study type: Cross-sectional analysis of a longitudinal study
exposure: stay in the same room during labor, delivery, and postpartum
adoption of non-lithotomy position in the delivery
score of the Brazilian Association of Market Research Institutes
use of non-pharmacological methods for pain relief
presence of a companion during labor
Presence of a companion during labor and delivery
source of payment for the delivery
outcome: Use of best practices during delivery care (e.g., supply of liquids and food, non-pharmacological pain relief methods, skin-to-skin contact)
Use of non-recommended practices (e.g., Kristeller maneuver, trichotomy, enema)
cohort: 2,070 women in the South region of Brazil who went into labor
finding: The presence of a companion during labor and delivery was associated with increased use of beneficial practices and a reduction in some unnecessary interventions, but not all.
mod_finding: The presence of a companion was associated with a higher cesarean section rate (aPR = 2.43).
